material.text: opencode-context-trimmer: An opencode plugin that trims upstream conversation context on long sessions to cut token cost, with a cache-aware gate and on-disk config.

type=plugin source=npm:opencode-context-trimmer created=2026-08-24T17:25:23.096Z firstSeen=2026-11-03T14:29:15.298Z published=2026-10-11T07:24:06.254Z maintainers=hdoer repoId=1345141296 stars=1 npm30d=?

# ⛲ context-trimmer ### Give [opencode](https://opencode.ai) an "infinite context" Never hit the context-window ceiling, no matter how long the session runs. The full history stays on disk; the model fetches it back on demand. [![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/opencode-context-trimmer?color=cb3837&logo=npm)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/opencode-context-trimmer) [![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](./LICENSE) [![opencode plugin](https://img.shields.io/badge/opencode-plugin-000000)](https://opencode.ai/docs/plugins/) [![runtime](https://img.shields.io/badge/runtime-Bun-f9f1e1?logo=bun)](https://bun.sh) **English** · [简体中文](./README.zh-CN.md)
🌊
Infinite context
Keep chatting — never cut off by the context limit		 💸
No wasted spend
Old history isn't resent, so it isn't re-billed		 ⚡
Zero latency
Instant, local — no extra model call		 🎯
Cache-safe
Doesn't break the prompt cache		 🔎
Always recallable
Trimmed content is fetchable on demand, even across projects
--- ## 60-second start ```jsonc // ~/.config/opencode/opencode.json { "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json", "plugin": ["opencode-context-trimmer"] } ``` Restart opencode — done. Works out of the box with no configuration. To tune it, see [Configuration](#configuration). --- ## Why opencode is **stateless** toward the model: every request resends the entire history. The longer the session, the more tokens are resent — tens of thousands, hundreds of thousands — until one request `exceeds the model context window` and the conversation stops dead. And every one of those resends is **billed, for real money**. The longer the session, the more stale old tool output you keep re-uploading, the more input tokens pile up and the higher the bill climbs. context-trimmer trims that redundancy in place before the request goes out — **tokens that are trimmed aren't sent, and what isn't sent isn't billed**. It won't make your total cost go *down*, but it tames the "pricier the longer you chat" runaway curve and keeps a long session's cost in a roughly stable band. The common "compaction/summarization" approach makes an **extra model call** to produce a summary: it costs money, adds latency, and mangles the original into a lossy digest. context-trimmer takes another road — **pure message rewriting** — trimming redundant turns in place before sending, with no model call and no loss of the original. | | Compaction/summary | **context-trimmer** | |---|---|---| | Extra token cost | ❌ A model call every time | ✅ Zero | | Extra latency | ❌ One more model round-trip | ✅ Instant, local | | Fidelity | ❌ Lossy digest | ✅ Original kept in full on disk | | Prompt cache | ❌ Prefix rewritten, invalidated | ✅ Sticky boundary, intact | | Information recovery | ❌ Cannot be restored | ✅ Fetched back via `context_recall` | ### It follows the "principle of locality" What the model needs most is almost always the **most recent turns**; the older something is, the less it gets referenced. Trimming therefore mirrors a CPU's multi-level cache: **recent turns** stay in fast memory (sent in full), **earlier turns** are demoted to a summary, and **distant turns** are paged back to main memory (local disk), fetched on demand with `context_recall`. A tiny recall cost buys a context that feels effectively "infinite." ## How it works ![turn-window trimming strategy diagram](docs/assets/turn-window.png) The plugin hooks `experimental.chat.messages.transform` (the point where outgoing messages can be rewritten) and applies a pluggable **strategy**. The built-in, default, and only strategy is `turn-window`: - A **turn** = one or more consecutive user messages plus the assistant messages that answer them. Consecutive user messages are merged into one turn (to absorb messages "queued up" mid-turn). - Trimming triggers when the active turn count exceeds `threshold`: - the most recent `recentFullTurns` turns are **kept in full** (user input + tool loop + final answer); - the `priorTrimmedTurns` turns before those keep only **user input + the assistant's final text** (the tool loop is dropped); - everything older is **dropped** (breadcrumbs may be kept — see below). - The trim boundary is **sticky**: pinned at `c - (recentFullTurns + priorTrimmedTurns)`, it stays put as the conversation grows so the serialized prefix remains byte-for-byte stable, which keeps the upstream prompt cache intact. The boundary only jumps forward when the active turn count exceeds `threshold` again (subject to the cache gate and hard cap below). After trimming, a notice is merged into the first retained user message, telling the model that earlier context was trimmed and how to fetch it back (see the tool below). ### Breadcrumbs (keeping summaries of dropped user messages) > The name "breadcrumbs" comes from the fairy tale *Hansel and Gretel*: before > being led into the forest, the siblings scatter breadcrumbs along the path so > they can follow the trail home. The idea here is the same — once the full > history is dropped, we leave behind a short summary (a truncated "crumb") of > each old user message, so the model can follow the trail and recall "what we > talked about earlier" instead of going blank. The most recent handful of **user messages** in the dropped region are kept as short "breadcrumbs," merged into that notice, so even without the full history the model has a thread to follow and doesn't lose the plot entirely. - `breadcrumbUserMessages`: how many of the most recent user messages in the dropped region to keep (default `100`, `0` disables). - `breadcrumbMaxTokens`: how many tokens to keep per message; longer ones are truncated with an ellipsis (default `100`). #### Truncation rules Each breadcrumb is truncated by **token** count (estimated at 1 token ≈ 3.5 UTF-8 bytes, converted to a byte budget), without relying on any tokenizer library: - Bytes are accumulated character by character; when adding a character would **exceed** the budget, it stops before that character. - **Never splits a character in half**: the cut always lands on a character boundary — a multi-byte character (a 3-byte Chinese character, or a surrogate pair like an emoji) is kept whole or dropped whole, so the result is always valid UTF-8. - When truncation happens, an ellipsis `…` is appended. For example, with a 3-token budget (≈10 bytes) and content `帮我修复登录` (3 bytes per character): it keeps `帮我修` (9 bytes); the 4th character would reach 12 bytes and exceed the budget, so it's truncated to `帮我修 …`. #### The assembled notice Once trimming triggers, the plugin joins the "breadcrumb block" and the "trim notice" with a blank line into one synthetic text part (`id: context-trimmer-notice`) prepended to the **first retained user message** (no extra message is added). With the default config, and when earlier messages were actually dropped, the inserted text looks like: ```text [context-trimmer] Summaries of earlier user messages that were trimmed (each truncated, as recall hints only): 1. Help me fix the error on the login page — clicking submit returns a 500 … 2. Which file holds the database connection pool config … 3. Make that function async, then add retries … [context-trimmer] Earlier context has been trimmed, but the full history is still saved in full and can be searched anytime. When you need the trimmed-away information, call the context_recall tool to fetch the original text: - query: keywords to search for; space-separated words are AND-matched (case-insensitive). - scope: where to search — a keyword or a session id. "session" (default): this session only, fastest and most relevant. "project": every session in the current project (including subagent child sessions). "all": every session across all projects on the machine — expensive, use ONLY when the user explicitly asks to search across projects, don't escalate on your own. Or pass a session id (e.g. "ses_...") to search exactly that one session. No need to confirm any path or database location — just call context_recall. ``` Composition and edge cases: - **Breadcrumb block**: a one-line heading + a numbered list, each item the truncated text of a dropped user message; it lists at most `breadcrumbUserMessages` items (default 100), each truncated to `breadcrumbMaxTokens` (default 100). It appears only when messages were dropped and `breadcrumbUserMessages > 0`. - **Trim notice**: tells the model that context was trimmed and how to fetch it back with `context_recall`. Customizable via the `notice` config option; set it to `""` to disable. - If both are empty, no notice is inserted and messages are left untouched. Because the wording is constant, when the sticky boundary is stable the serialized prefix stays byte-for-byte stable and the upstream prompt cache isn't broken. ### Cache-aware gate (Re)triggering a trim reshapes the prefix and invalidates the upstream prompt cache (which typically has a ~5-minute TTL). `cacheAwareMinutes` defers the trigger until the session has been idle for at least that many minutes — by which point the cache has already expired, so no extra cache-miss cost is paid. Trimming is deferred during active conversation; set it to `0` to trim as soon as the threshold is hit. #### Overflow hard cap (`hardTriggerTurns`) The cache gate has a risk: during **sustained high-frequency work**, every request's gap is shorter than `cacheAwareMinutes`, so the gate defers the trigger indefinitely — the sticky boundary never advances, the retained region grows by one turn each round without bound, and eventually it blows past the model's context window (surfacing as the upstream returning `The request exceeds the model context window`). `hardTriggerTurns` is the overflow backstop: when the active turn count exceeds it, the boundary is force-advanced even if the cache is still "hot" (trading one cache miss for avoiding a hard overflow). The default `0` means auto `threshold * 2`. ### Session attribution (subagent safety) The `experimental.chat.messages.transform` hook receives empty input and can't see the current session id, so the plugin bridges each session's model info via `chat.params` into a store keyed by session id. The key point: when transform fires, it locates the context **by the real `info.sessionID` in the message list**, not by guessing from the "most recent `chat.params`". This is critical for **subagents**. A subagent runs in the same process as its parent session, interleaved: while the subtask runs it points the "most recent session" pointer at the child session; when the parent session then takes over, guessing by "most recent session" would hand it the **child's** context, so the parent's sticky boundary can't be found under the wrong key — trimming silently fails, the entire untrimmed history is sent as-is, and eventually it blows past the context window. Locating by the message's real sessionID means the parent always finds its own boundary on takeover and trims normally. ## Installation ### Option 1: npm package (recommended) Add the package name to the `plugin` array in your opencode config (`~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` or a project-level `opencode.json`); opencode installs it with Bun automatically at startup: ```json { "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json", "plugin": ["opencode-context-trimmer"] } ``` ### Option 2: local file opencode also auto-discovers plugins under `~/.config/opencode/plugin/` (or `plugins/`). Copy the plugin entry file **and its directory** over together: ```bash mkdir -p ~/.config/opencode/plugin cp -R context-trimmer.ts context-trimmer ~/.config/opencode/plugin/ ``` ### Confirm it loaded Restart opencode, then check the log: ```bash grep "\[context-trimmer\]" ~/.local/share/opencode/log/opencode.log ``` You should see a `plugin loaded version=…` line — use it to confirm the plugin is active and which version is running (after an upgrade or reinstall, check it to verify the new build actually took effect). Each time a request is trimmed you'll also see a `trimmed before=… after=…` line. `@opencode-ai/plugin` and `@opencode-ai/sdk` are provided by the opencode runtime — no manual install needed. ## Configuration Optional. Built-in defaults are used when no config file is present. To customize, create: ``` $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/opencode/context-trimmer.json # default: ~/.config/opencode/context-trimmer.json ``` ```json { "enabled": true, "threshold": 20, "recentFullTurns": 5, "priorTrimmedTurns": 5, "cacheAwareMinutes": 5, "hardTriggerTurns": 0, "breadcrumbUserMessages": 100, "breadcrumbMaxTokens": 100 } ``` | Field | Default | Meaning | |------|--------|------| | `enabled` | `true` | Master switch. When `false`, no request is altered. | | `threshold` | `20` | (Re)trigger trimming when the active turn count exceeds this. | | `recentFullTurns` | `5` | Number of most recent turns kept in full. | | `priorTrimmedTurns` | `5` | Turns before those that keep only "user input + final output". | | `cacheAwareMinutes` | `5` | (Re)trigger only after the session has been idle this many minutes (cache already expired). `0` disables the gate. | | `hardTriggerTurns` | `0` | Overflow hard cap: when the active turn count exceeds it, force-advance the boundary regardless of the cache gate. `0` means auto `threshold * 2`. | | `breadcrumbUserMessages` | `100` | How many of the most recent user messages in the dropped region to keep as breadcrumbs. `0` disables. | | `breadcrumbMaxTokens` | `100` | Max tokens kept per breadcrumb (converted at ≈3.5 bytes/token, cut at a character boundary). | Changes take effect on the **next request** — no restart needed (the file is re-read via an mtime cache). A missing or malformed file falls back to defaults; a single invalid field falls back to just that field's default without affecting the rest. ### Example: looser trimming Triggers later and keeps more — suited to cases that value context completeness over token cost: ```json { "enabled": true, "threshold": 30, "recentFullTurns": 8, "priorTrimmedTurns": 8, "cacheAwareMinutes": 5 } ``` ## Fetching back trimmed history Trimming only reshapes the *upstream request* — opencode still keeps the full history on disk. The plugin registers a `context_recall` tool so the model can fetch trimmed-away content on demand: - `query` — keywords; space-separated words are AND-matched (case-insensitive). - `scope` — where to search; a single overloaded value, either a keyword or a concrete session id, narrow to wide: - `session` (default) — the current session only, fastest and most relevant. - `project` — every session in the current project (sibling + subagent child sessions). - `all` — every session across **all projects** on this machine. Can be slow (it scans the whole history when nothing matches), so use it only when you explicitly ask to search across projects; the model won't escalate to `all` on its own just because a narrower scope found nothing. - a specific session id (e.g. `ses_...`) — search exactly that one session, the most precise lookup. Any value other than the three keywords is treated as a session id. `scope: all` has a handy use: when you remember discussing a topic but can't recall which project/session it was in — explicitly ask the model to search across all projects with `all` and it can pull that conversation back without you digging through history. ## Extending Add a strategy file under `context-trimmer/strategies/`, implement the `Strategy` interface (`enabled(ctx)` + `apply(messages, ctx)`), and register it in `context-trimmer/strategies/index.ts`. Strategies run in order, each seeing the previous one's output; a strategy that throws is skipped (fail-open), so a buggy strategy can never break a request. ## Project layout ``` context-trimmer.ts Plugin entry (hooks + tool registration) context-trimmer/ config.ts Global config loader (mtime cache, fail-safe) context.ts Per-session model/provider info bridged from chat.params logger.ts Fail-safe logger over client.app.log pipeline.ts Runs enabled strategies in order (fail-open) globals.d.ts Minimal ambient declarations (no @types/node) strategies/ types.ts Strategy contract index.ts Strategy registry turn-window.ts Sticky turn-window strategy tools/ recall.ts context_recall tool ``` Tests live next to the files they cover, named `*.test.ts`, run with `bun run .test.ts`.

# ⛲ context-trimmer ### 给 [opencode](https://opencode.ai) 装上「无限上下文」 任意长会话也不撞上下文窗口上限。完整历史留在本地，模型按需取回。 [![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/opencode-context-trimmer?color=cb3837&logo=npm)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/opencode-context-trimmer) [![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](./LICENSE) [![opencode plugin](https://img.shields.io/badge/opencode-plugin-000000)](https://opencode.ai/docs/plugins/) [![runtime](https://img.shields.io/badge/runtime-Bun-f9f1e1?logo=bun)](https://bun.sh) **简体中文** · [English](./README.md)
🌊
无限上下文
一直聊下去，不会被上下文上限打断		 💸
不花冤枉钱
旧历史不反复重发，就不反复计费		 ⚡
零延时
本地瞬时完成，没有额外的模型调用		 🎯
缓存无损
不破坏 prompt 缓存		 🔎
可随时召回
裁掉的内容仍可按需取回，还能跨项目检索
--- ## 60 秒上手 ```jsonc // ~/.config/opencode/opencode.json { "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json", "plugin": ["opencode-context-trimmer"] } ``` 重启 opencode，完成。默认开箱即用，无需配置。想微调见 [配置](#配置)。 --- ## 为什么 opencode 对模型**无状态**：每次请求都重发整段历史。会话越长，重复发送的 token 越多—— 几万、几十万，直到某次请求 `exceeds the model context window`，对话戛然而止。 而这每一次重发，都在**真金白银地计费**。会话越长，反复上送早已无关的旧工具输出， 输入 token 就越滚越多，账单随之水涨船高。context-trimmer 在发出前就地裁掉这些冗余—— **裁掉的 token 不上送，不上送就不计费**。它不会让总成本下降，但能摁住「越聊越贵」的失控曲线， 让长会话的开销维持在一个大致稳定的区间。 常见的「压缩/总结」方案要**额外调一次模型**生成摘要：花钱、增延时、还把原文揉成有损概要。 context-trimmer 走另一条路——**纯消息重写**，发出前就地裁掉冗余轮次，不调模型、不丢原文。 | | 压缩/总结 | **context-trimmer** | |---|---|---| | 额外 token 费用 | ❌ 每次都调模型 | ✅ 零 | | 额外延时 | ❌ 额外调一次模型 | ✅ 本地瞬时完成 | | 原文保真 | ❌ 有损概要 | ✅ 完整留本地 | | prompt 缓存 | ❌ 前缀重写、失效 | ✅ 粘性边界、无损 | | 信息找回 | ❌ 无法还原 | ✅ `context_recall` 取回 | ### 符合「局部性原理」 模型当前最需要的，几乎总是**最近几轮**；越久远越少被引用。裁剪因此恰如 CPU 多级缓存： **最近轮次**常驻快表（完整发送），**较早轮次**降级摘要，**久远轮次**退回主存（本地磁盘）， 需要时再用 `context_recall` 换页取回。用极小的召回成本，换一个看似「无限大」的上下文。 ## 工作原理 ![turn-window 裁剪策略示意图](docs/assets/turn-window.zh-CN.png) 插件挂载 `experimental.chat.messages.transform` 钩子（重写待发送消息的时机）， 应用一个可插拔的**策略（strategy）**。内置且默认的唯一策略是 `turn-window`： - 一**轮（turn）** = 一条或多条连续的用户消息，加上回应它们的助手消息。 连续的用户消息会被合并成一轮（以吸收轮次中途"排队"发出的消息）。 - 当活跃轮数超过 `threshold` 时触发裁剪： - 最近 `recentFullTurns` 轮**完整保留**（用户输入 + 工具循环 + 最终回答）； - 再往前的 `priorTrimmedTurns` 轮只保留**用户输入 + 助手最终文本**（丢弃工具循环）； - 更早的全部**丢弃**（但可保留面包屑，见下）。 - 裁剪边界是**粘性的**：固定在 `c - (recentFullTurns + priorTrimmedTurns)`， 随对话增长保持不动，使序列化后的前缀保持逐字节稳定，从而不破坏上游的 prompt 缓存。 只有当活跃轮数再次超过 `threshold` 时，边界才会向前跳（受缓存门控与硬上限约束，见下）。 裁剪后会在第一条保留的用户消息里合并一段提示，告诉模型较早的上下文已被裁剪， 以及如何取回（见下方工具）。 ### 面包屑（保留被丢弃的用户消息摘要） > "面包屑" 这个名字来自童话《韩塞尔与格蕾特》：兄妹俩被带进森林前，沿路撒下面包屑， > 好顺着这串痕迹找到回家的路。这里的道理相同——完整历史被丢弃后，我们沿途留下每条旧 > 用户消息的简短摘要（截断过的"碎屑"），让模型顺着线索回忆起"早先聊过什么"，而不至于断片。 被丢弃区域里最近的若干条**用户消息**会被保留为简短"面包屑"，合并进那段提示里， 让模型即便看不到完整历史也有一条回忆线索、不至于完全断片。 - `breadcrumbUserMessages`：保留被丢弃区域中最近多少条用户消息（默认 `100`，`0` 关闭）。 - `breadcrumbMaxTokens`：每条最多保留多少个 token，超出截断并加省略号（默认 `100`）。 #### 截断规则 每条面包屑按 **token** 数截断（按 1 token ≈ 3.5 个 UTF-8 字节估算，换算成字节预算）， 不依赖任何分词库： - 逐字符累加字节数，当加上某个字符会**超过**预算时，就在该字符之前停下。 - **绝不切半个字符**：截断点始终落在字符边界上，一个多字节字符（如 3 字节的汉字、 或 emoji 这类代理对）要么整体保留、要么整体丢弃，结果始终是合法 UTF-8。 - 发生截断时在末尾追加省略号 `…`。 例如预算 3 token（≈10 字节）、内容 `帮我修复登录`（每字 3 字节）：留下 `帮我修`（9 字节）， 第 4 个字会到 12 字节超预算，于是截断为 `帮我修 …`。 #### 组装后的完整提示词 裁剪触发后，插件会把「面包屑块」和「裁剪提示」用一个空行拼接，作为一个合成文本段 （`id: context-trimmer-notice`）插到**第一条保留用户消息**的最前面（不新增额外消息）。 默认配置下、且确有更早消息被丢弃时，插入的完整文本形如： ```text [context-trimmer] Summaries of earlier user messages that were trimmed (each truncated, as recall hints only): 1. Help me fix the error on the login page — clicking submit returns a 500 … 2. Which file holds the database connection pool config … 3. Make that function async, then add retries … [context-trimmer] Earlier context has been trimmed, but the full history is still saved in full and can be searched anytime. When you need the trimmed-away information, call the context_recall tool to fetch the original text: - query: keywords to search for; space-separated words are AND-matched (case-insensitive). - scope: where to search — a keyword or a session id. "session" (default): this session only, fastest and most relevant. "project": every session in the current project (including subagent child sessions). "all": every session across all projects on the machine — expensive, use ONLY when the user explicitly asks to search across projects, don't escalate on your own. Or pass a session id (e.g. "ses_...") to search exactly that one session. No need to confirm any path or database location — just call context_recall. ``` 组成与边界情况： - **面包屑块**：一行标题 + 编号列表，每条是被丢弃用户消息的截断文本；最多列出 `breadcrumbUserMessages` 条（默认 100），每条截到 `breadcrumbMaxTokens`（默认 100）。 仅当有消息被丢弃且 `breadcrumbUserMessages > 0` 时出现。 - **裁剪提示**：告知模型上下文已被裁剪，以及如何用 `context_recall` 取回。可用 `notice` 配置项自定义；设为 `""` 可关闭。 - 若两者都为空，则不插入任何提示，消息保持原样。 因为文案恒定，粘性边界稳定时序列化前缀保持逐字节稳定，不会破坏上游 prompt 缓存。 ### 缓存感知门控 （重新）触发裁剪会重塑前缀、使上游 prompt 缓存失效（缓存通常有约 5 分钟的 TTL）。 `cacheAwareMinutes` 会推迟触发，直到会话空闲至少这么多分钟——那时缓存本就已过期， 因此不会付出额外的缓存未命中代价。活跃对话期间裁剪会被推迟；设为 `0` 则命中阈值即裁。 #### 硬上限兜底（`hardTriggerTurns`） 缓存门控有一个风险：**持续高频工作**时，每次请求的间隔都小于 `cacheAwareMinutes`， 门控会把触发无限期推迟——粘性边界永不前移，保留区每轮增长一轮、无上限累积， 最终撑爆模型上下文窗口（表现为上游返回 `The request exceeds the model context window`）。 `hardTriggerTurns` 是防溢出兜底：当活跃轮数超过它时，即便缓存仍"热"也强制前移边界 （以一次缓存未命中换取避免硬性溢出）。默认 `0` 表示自动取 `threshold * 2`。 ### 会话归属（子 agent 安全） `experimental.chat.messages.transform` 钩子的入参是空的，拿不到当前会话 id，所以插件 通过 `chat.params` 把每个会话的模型信息桥接到一个按会话 id 建键的存储里。关键在于： transform 触发时**以消息列表里真实的 `info.sessionID` 为准**来定位上下文，而不是用"最近 一次 `chat.params`"去猜。 这一点对 **subagent（子任务）** 至关重要。子 agent 与父会话跑在同一进程里、交错执行： 子任务运行时会把"最近会话"指针指向子会话；父会话随后接手时，若按"最近会话"去猜，就会 拿到**子会话**的上下文，导致父会话的粘性边界在错误的 key 下查不到——裁剪静默失效、整段 未裁剪的历史被原样上送，最终撑爆上下文窗口。改用消息真实 sessionID 定位后，父会话接手 时总能查到自己的边界，正常裁剪。 ## 安装 ### 方式一：npm 包（推荐） 在 opencode 配置文件（`~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` 或项目级 `opencode.json`） 的 `plugin` 数组里加入包名，opencode 启动时会自动用 Bun 安装： ```json { "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json", "plugin": ["opencode-context-trimmer"] } ``` ### 方式二：本地文件 opencode 也会自动发现 `~/.config/opencode/plugin/`（或 `plugins/`）下的插件。 把插件入口文件**及其目录**一起复制过去： ```bash mkdir -p ~/.config/opencode/plugin cp -R context-trimmer.ts context-trimmer ~/.config/opencode/plugin/ ``` ### 确认已加载 重启 opencode，然后查看日志： ```bash grep "\[context-trimmer\]" ~/.local/share/opencode/log/opencode.log ``` 你应能看到一行 `plugin loaded version=…`——借此可确认插件已激活、且跑的是哪个版本 （升级或重装后用它核对是否真的生效）。每当裁剪一次请求时，还会看到一行 `trimmed before=… after=…`。 `@opencode-ai/plugin` 与 `@opencode-ai/sdk` 由 opencode 运行时提供——无需手动安装。 ## 配置 可选。没有配置文件时使用内置默认值。要自定义，创建： ``` $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/opencode/context-trimmer.json # 默认：~/.config/opencode/context-trimmer.json ``` ```json { "enabled": true, "threshold": 20, "recentFullTurns": 5, "priorTrimmedTurns": 5, "cacheAwareMinutes": 5, "hardTriggerTurns": 0, "breadcrumbUserMessages": 100, "breadcrumbMaxTokens": 100 } ``` | 字段 | 默认值 | 含义 | |------|--------|------| | `enabled` | `true` | 总开关。`false` 时不改动任何请求。 | | `threshold` | `20` | 活跃轮数超过此值时（重新）触发裁剪。 | | `recentFullTurns` | `5` | 最近完整保留的轮数。 | | `priorTrimmedTurns` | `5` | 再往前只保留"用户输入 + 最终输出"的轮数。 | | `cacheAwareMinutes` | `5` | 会话空闲达到这么多分钟（缓存已过期）后才（重新）触发。`0` 关闭该门控。 | | `hardTriggerTurns` | `0` | 防溢出硬上限：活跃轮数超过它时无视缓存门控强制前移边界。`0` 表示自动取 `threshold * 2`。 | | `breadcrumbUserMessages` | `100` | 被丢弃区域中保留为面包屑的最近用户消息条数。`0` 关闭。 | | `breadcrumbMaxTokens` | `100` | 每条面包屑最多保留的 token 数（按 ≈3.5 字节/token 换算，在字符边界处截断）。 | 改动在**下一次请求**即生效——无需重启（文件通过 mtime 缓存重新读取）。 文件缺失或格式错误时回落到默认值；单个非法字段只回落该字段的默认值，不影响其余字段。 ### 示例：更宽松的裁剪 更晚触发、保留更多——适合更看重上下文完整性、不那么在意 token 成本的场景： ```json { "enabled": true, "threshold": 30, "recentFullTurns": 8, "priorTrimmedTurns": 8, "cacheAwareMinutes": 5 } ``` ## 取回被裁剪的历史 裁剪只重塑*上游请求*——opencode 仍在本地保留完整历史。插件注册了一个 `context_recall` 工具，让模型可以按需取回被裁掉的内容： - `query` —— 关键词；以空格分隔的多个词按"与"匹配（大小写不敏感）。 - `scope` —— 查哪里；单个重载参数，既可传关键字，也可直接传会话 id，从窄到宽： - `session`（默认）—— 仅当前会话，最快、最相关。 - `project` —— 当前项目的全部会话（含兄弟会话与 subagent 子会话）。 - `all` —— 本机**所有项目**的全部会话。可能较慢（无命中时会扫全库）， 因此仅在你明确要求跨项目查找时才用；模型不会因为窄范围没查到就自行升级到 `all`。 - 会话 id（形如 `ses_...`）—— 只查这一个会话，最精准的定点查法。 非上述三个关键字的值都会被当作会话 id 处理。 `scope: all` 有个顺手的用法：有时你记得聊过某个话题，却想不起在哪个项目/会话里—— 明确让模型用 `all` 跨所有项目按关键词检索，就能把那段对话捞回来，不必翻遍历史。 ## 扩展 在 `context-trimmer/strategies/` 下新增一个策略文件，实现 `Strategy` 接口 （`enabled(ctx)` + `apply(messages, ctx)`），并在 `context-trimmer/strategies/index.ts` 中注册。策略按顺序执行，每个都能看到前一个的输出；抛异常的策略会被跳过（fail-open）， 因此一个有缺陷的策略永远不会破坏请求。 ## 项目结构 ``` context-trimmer.ts 插件入口（钩子 + 工具注册） context-trimmer/ config.ts 全局配置加载器（mtime 缓存、fail-safe） context.ts 从 chat.params 桥接的每会话模型/provider 信息 logger.ts 基于 client.app.log 的 fail-safe 日志器 pipeline.ts 按顺序运行已启用策略（fail-open） globals.d.ts 最小 ambient 声明（不引入 @types/node） strategies/ types.ts 策略契约 index.ts 策略注册表 turn-window.ts 粘性 turn-window 策略 tools/ recall.ts context_recall 工具 ``` 测试与被测文件放在一起，命名为 `*.test.ts`，用 `bun run .test.ts` 运行。
